name: MemAC (Memory Answer Choice Translation)
text:
1
MemAC (Memory Answer Choice Translation)
5 QUESTIONS
Instructions

NOTE: MemAC is a multi-day series of workouts using previously-seen LR and RC sections that progress through five levels as you meet certain benchmarks. Each level and benchmark is defined below. MemAC can be completed as a full section* or by completing as much MemAC as possible in 1-3 hour blocks.

Start MemAC at Level 1, or from wherever you left off previously.

Level 1 MemAC means that you will be performing the answer choice Translation process defined in the Level 1 instructions below. If you are on a later Level, follow the corresponding instructions below.

To Level Up: Complete the full MemAC process defined in your Level instructions without having to peek at the answer choices to accurately remember them on 10 questions in a row.

For example, if you correctly recap all the answer choices on 10 questions in a row without having to peek on Level 1, move to Level 2 on the next question.

Each time you complete one full section of MemAC, complete a MemAC Live Check-In Question(defined below).

MemAC Live Check-In Question

Complete a full LR question according to the Full LR Process. 

Just translate and quip the answers normally. Do not do MemAC.

After choosing your answer, attempt to translate all the answer choices from memory. 

Write down how many answers you're able to translate from memory on each Live Check-In Question.

Compare the number of answers you're able to translate from memory across all your Live Check-In Questions to measure your progress.

MemAC Level 1: One answer at a time

When you beat Level 1, progress to Level 2.

Read, translate, and quip answer choice A.

Repeat the Translation of A from memory.

Read, translate, and quip answer choice B.

Repeat the Translation of A and B from memory.

Read, translate, and quip answer choice C.

Repeat the Translation of A, B, C from memory.

Read, translate, and quip answer choice D.

Repeat the Translation of A, B, C, D from memory.

Read, translate, and quip answer choice E.

Repeat the Translation of A, B, C, D, E from memory.

MemAC Level 2: Two answers at a time

When you beat Level 2, progress to Level 3.

Read, translate, and quip answer choice A.

Read, translate, and quip answer choice B.

Repeat the Translation of A and B from memory.

Read, translate, and quip answer choice C.

Read, translate, and quip answer choice D.

Repeat the Translation of A, B, C, D from memory.

Read, translate, and quip answer choice E.

Repeat the Translation of A, B, C, D, E from memory.

MemAC Level 3: Three answers at a time

When you beat Level 3, progress to Level 4.

Read, translate, and quip answer choice A.

Read, translate, and quip answer choice B.

Read, translate, and quip answer choice C.

Repeat the Translation of A, B, C from memory.

Read, translate, and quip answer choice D.

Read, translate, and quip answer choice E.

Repeat the Translation of A, B, C, D, E from memory.

MemAC Level 4: Four answers at a time

When you beat Level 4, progress to Level 5.

Read, translate, and quip answer choice A.

Read, translate, and quip answer choice B.

Read, translate, and quip answer choice C.

Read, translate, and quip answer choice D.

Repeat the Translation of A, B, C, D from memory.

Read, translate, and quip answer choice E.

Repeat the Translation of A, B, C, D, E from memory.

MemAC Level 5: Five answers at a time

When you beat Level 5, congratulations! You've beaten MemAC!

Read, translate, and quip answer choice A.

Read, translate, and quip answer choice B.

Read, translate, and quip answer choice C.

Read, translate, and quip answer choice D.

Read, translate, and quip answer choice E.

Repeat the Translation of A, B, C, D, E from memory.

SEE FULL WORKOUT DETAILS

name: Vocabulary Translation Drill
text:
2
Vocabulary Translation Drill
1 SECTION
Instructions

Translate and quip the passage or stimulus*.

If you encounter a word you are unsure of, highlight it.

Finish the passage or stimulus.

Be sure to highlight ALL the words you're unsure of.

If you wouldn't bet money on the definition of the word, that means you are unsure of the definition of that word.

Add the highlighted words to your Vocab Tracker and write in the definitions according to the instructions outlined in the How to Learn Vocab Without AI video.

Restart the Vocabulary Translation Drill on the same stimulus or passage now that you know what the words mean.

Continue this pattern for the entire section.

SEE FULL WORKOUT DETAILS

name: Cappuccino RC Translation Drill
text:
3
Cappuccino RC Translation Drill
1 SECTION
Instructions

NOTE: Cappuccino is similar to Decaf, except instead of recapping all of your Translations after finishing with each paragraph, you’ll be looking back at the text to confirm your Translations.

Read, translate, and quip paragraph 1*. Do it just like LR.

Look away from paragraph 1 and recap the FULL TRANSLATION of paragraph 1 silently.

Take a few seconds to confirm your Translation with the paragraph you just read.

In this step, you are not rereading from scratch. 

You're confirming the Translation you already have is right. 

This style of confirming your Translation with the text applies to every confirmation you ever do on RC.

Read, translate, and quip paragraph 2. Do it just like LR.

Look away from paragraph 2 and recap the FULL TRANSLATION of paragraph 2 silently.

Take a few seconds to confirm your Translation with all the text you've read of the passage so far.

This confirmation step will include all the paragraphs you've read so far.

Repeat this pattern for all remaining paragraphs.

OPTIONAL: Look away and recap the FULL TRANSLATION of the entire passage silently.

This step is optional, but you should do it when you first begin Cappuccino RC Translation Drills and periodically afterward, just to confirm that you can.

Complete this same process on all remaining passages in the section.

SEE FULL WORKOUT DETAILS

name: Write In
text:
4
Write In
1 SECTION
Instructions

NOTE: The Write In replaces the Mission step of the Full LR Process.

Read and translate the stimulus in chunks*. 

Quip each chunk of the stimulus after you translate.

Continue until the end of the stimulus.

Mark the conclusion.

Immediately proceed to the CLIR after your final quip of the stimulus (or the final quip is the CLIR).

Read the question stem, identify the question type and whether the question is Powerful-Provable.

Write in a correct answer to the question.

Make the Write In answer sound like a real answer choice, not a messy note.

On every individual answer choice:

Read, translate, and quip the answer choice.

Investigate whether this answer choice meets the question type's Back Up Plan.

If you think this answer meets the Back-Up Plan question, highlight the first word of the answer.

If you are not sure whether this answer meets the Back-Up Plan question, leave it open.

If you know this answer doesn't meet the Back-Up Plan question, cross it out.

Choose amongst the open and highlighted answer choices.

Hyperskip, if needed.

Aim to hyperskip 5-7 questions per section.

Use any remaining time to return to your hyperskips.

SEE FULL WORKOUT DETAILS

name: Vocab Training
text:
6
Vocab Training
Instructions

Highlight any word you wouldn't bet your LSAT score on during all LSAT sections and during all Extracurricular Reading.

These highlighted words are your vocab words.

Harvest all the vocab words you've highlighted after your section or reading is complete.

Harvesting your words means writing down each of your vocab words in a tracker. You can use my template or create a simple Google Sheet for this.

Always harvest your vocab words the same day that you highlight them.

To further optimize your vocab harvesting, watch the How to Harvest Vocab Words video.

Practice your vocab words daily for at least 10 minutes.

To practice, follow the procedures outlined in the How to Learn Vocab Without AI video or the How to Learn Vocab: AI Supercharged Edition video.

10 minutes of practice is a minimum, not a maximum. If you have a 100+ number of vocab words to learn, do not be afraid to practice for a longer period of time.

SEE FULL WORKOUT DETAILS

name: Camo Review
text:
7
Camo Review
Instructions

When you finish an LR or RC section in LawHub, do not press Complete Section. Instead, write down your answers.

Use Self-Paced Mode on all LR and RC sections. Never use Exam Mode.

At least 24 hours later, enter your answers into Camo Review.

Do not check your answers against the answer key before entering your answers into Camo Review.

Camo Review will give you a list of questions to return to.

This list includes all of your wrong answers and an unknown number of decoy correct answers.

Reattempt all of the questions in your Camo Review from scratch. Attempt to do a better job on the question now than you did the first time.

Doing a better job means you should retranslate, requip, and re-CLIR the stimulus on LR or retranslate and requip the passage on RC. Retranslate every part of the question, consider every answer choice, and try to correct your process mistakes before choosing a new answer.

Enter all your new answers into Camo Review.

Camo Review will identify all your Misreads, Conceptual Gaps, Self-Doubt, and Self-Confidence answers.

Your Misreads, Conceptual Gaps, and Self-Doubt answers have been automatically added to your Wrong Answer Journal. Go to your Wrong Answer Journal now to immediately begin the Wrong Answer Journal process.

SEE FULL WORKOUT DETAILS

name: Wrong Answer Journal
text:
8
Wrong Answer Journal
Instructions

After you've Camoed your LR or RC section, begin the Wrong Answer Journaling process.

For each wrong answer, fill in the date you did the section, the question number that was wrong, and the answer you chose.

This information will already be filled in for you if you Camo using Loophole Online.

Fill in your Reason Missed column

In this column, write down what you did wrong that caused you to miss this question.

Ask yourself, "Why did I think that this wrong answer was right? Why did I think that this right answer was wrong?" Focus on changing the actions that enabled these mistaken judgments.

The first word of every entry in this column should be "I." 

Example: "I misidentified the question stem."

This will force you to reflect on what you did that caused you to choose the wrong answer and overlook the right answer.

Fill in your Solution column

In this column, write down what you will do differently to ensure you don't make this same mistake again.

Ask yourself, "What could I have done that would have made me realize in the moment that the wrong answer is wrong? What could I have done that would have made me realize in the moment that the right answer is right?"

The first words of every entry in this column should be "I will..." 

Example: "I will do Question Stem Training to improve my ability to correctly identify question types."

Frame your Solution Column as a direct response to the Reason Missed column.

Click here to go to your Wrong Answer Journal
